prices: 2026-11-05 close (stockanalysis.com; checked against a second source)
method: Implied return: the yearly return on the whole firm (debt plus equity) at which today’s enterprise value equals consensus revenue for the next fiscal year (calendar 2027 for most; NVIDIA’s year to Jan 2028; Broadcom’s year in progress), at a steady-state margin set by one rule, growing 5% a year after that. Enterprise value excludes leases, matching free cash flow measured after lease payments. It is compared with each company’s cost of capital: own bond yield (or the 10-year Treasury ≈4.8% plus 1 point for investment grade, plus 5 points for unrated), equity at debt plus 4 points, weighted by market value, 21% tax.
rule: Free cash flow held down by AI capex (Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Oracle)
Average net margin FY2020–22, before the boom
Cyclical: net margin swung more than 15 points over FY2020–25 for business reasons (NVIDIA, Micron). Swings from non-cash acquisition amortization (Broadcom, AMD) do not count
Average net margin FY2020–25 (NVIDIA shown as a range up to its latest margin)
15–25%, an assumption; shown as a range
verdict_rule: One cutoff for all: more than 2 points below its cost of capital = rich; more than 2 points above = cheap if forecasts hold; in between = about fair. The cutoff is wider than the rule-of-thumb noise (moving the equity premium by a point moves cost of capital by about a point).
limits: Net margin stands in for free-cash-flow margin: it is after interest and ignores the capex that growth needs, so it flatters capex-heavy firms (Oracle most).
Cost of equity is a rule of thumb (debt + 4 points), not a measured beta.
Mid-ramp landlords: next-year revenue understates signed leases.
Leases signed but not yet started (Oracle, CoreWeave) are not included.
Research, not investment advice. No position sizes.

policy.fleet_denominator: Epoch US frontier tracker, end-2028 H100e = 59.7M
notes: Ordinary slip is an assumption (E): sites with only a year-end placeholder date slip 25–50% of the time, dated ramps 10–20%, expanding sites 5–10%.

Policy shares and delay lengths are set per site by stage (E), and apply only to capacity that would not slip anyway: Texas’s grid pause exempts sites already approved and under construction; the state permit halt is broader.
New Mexico: Project Jupiter is under construction; its air permit for on-site generation is due ≈Nov 23. If denied, ≈1.4 GW more slips 6–8 quarters, close to a restart.
NVIDIA’s $105B guarantee sits on the PORTS-Pike campus in Ohio (leased to OpenAI), which Epoch does not track; not modelled.
A delay moves spend and revenue later; it does not remove them. It moves part of OpenAI’s 2028 funding gap into 2029.
Federal: Democratic majorities from Jan 3, 2027; a veto blocks a federal ban. No federal change is modelled.
